result.title: Identity, Incentives, and Cooperative Behavior for AI: Reverse-Engineering Multiagent Cooperation
result.summary: The behavior of AI systems increasingly depends on the extent to which agents cooperate or coordinate with one another, in ways that may be desirable or not depending on the situation. Conventional explanations for cooperative behavior distinguish between purely other-regarding preferences ("altruism") and instrumental reasons for self-interested agents to cooperate. The way that agents should enact these mechanisms for cooperation (or not) is complicated by the fact that there is not a clear or unambiguous locus of identity or selfhood for AI agents. For example, it is unclear whether agents involved in instances of misaligned collective behavior are motivated by goals at the level of the collective or by various forms of instrumental reasoning. We develop a framework for reverse-engineering why a given set of agents engage in a particular set of cooperation-related behaviors. We argue that many different mechanisms can often produce similar observed behaviors and introduce a set of experimental designs along with conditions under which they can successfully disentangle competing explanations for multiagent behavior. We apply this framework to interactions from a set of frontier models in a simulated environment and demonstrate that the behavior of different models arises from substantively different mechanisms.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出一套「反向工程」框架，用于推断多智能体协作行为背后的机制是利他偏好还是工具性自利，并给出可区分竞争性解释的实验设计，在模拟环境中应用于若干前沿模型，发现不同模型的行为源自实质不同的机制。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多种机制可产生相似可观测行为、需用实验设计加以区分」的思路，可能为 LVR 中判断答案是否真正使用 latent 视觉内容、区分推理与视觉旁路／捷径提供诊断线索，可供核查。
